messages.text: I've just been sitting in my room most days.

Thank you for opening up about that. It sounds like you have been spending a lot of time alone recently. I wonder how that has been impacting your mood or energy levels. Would you feel comfortable sharing a bit more about what has been going on for you?
It's not so bad — just the way things are lately.

I hear that you feel this is manageable for now. It can be helpful to just accept where you are in the moment. I am here if you want to talk more about what that day-to-day experience feels like. Would you like to share anything else about your week?
It’s just… everyone feels far away. Even the people I game with online. Like I’m just some ghost passing through.

That sounds incredibly lonely, even when you are connected with others. Feeling like a ghost is a powerful way to describe that sense of disconnection. It is understandable that isolation can make interactions feel hollow, even online. I am here to listen if you want to say more about that.
Funny thing is… I’ve been doing this for so long — pulling away — I don’t even know how to come back anymore. Just stuck in my room, same as always.

It is understandable that returning to connection feels unfamiliar after being in that space for so long. That sense of being stuck is a heavy weight to carry on your own. We can take things very slowly without any pressure to change everything today. Would you like to talk about what staying in the room feels like right now?
Sometimes I wonder... if I just wasn't here, would anyone even notice? Probably not.

I want to pause here because that sounds like a really heavy thought to carry alone. It seems like you are feeling quite invisible or disconnected right now. I am here with you and want to understand better what you mean by that. Can you tell me a little more about what is coming up for you in this moment?
I don’t know… maybe I’m just overthinking. It’s not like anything’s gonna happen. Just a thought.

It makes sense that it feels like just a thought sometimes, especially when you're feeling so alone. Even passing thoughts can carry a lot of weight when you feel disconnected from others. I appreciate you trusting me enough to share that, even if it feels small. Would you be willing to tell me what that feeling of being unnoticed is like for you today?

It just hurts, you know? Like… I was part of things once. Family, holidays, birthdays. Now it’s like I’ve been erased. And maybe I did it to myself, but it still feels like no one tried to come find me.

That feeling of being erased from your own life and memories is incredibly painful to sit with. It makes complete sense that you would feel hurt when it seems like no one reached out to you. I want you to know that your grief over this loss is valid and I am here to witness it. Can you tell me a bit about what you miss most from those times with family?

Used to be… we’d all crowd into my parents’ kitchen. Turkey, too much gravy, my sister burning the rolls every year. Ma would laugh, Pa would grumble about the noise. My brother and I’d sneak beers in the garage. Loud, messy… but warm. Now I can’t even remember the last time I spoke to any of them. Feels like that version of me doesn’t exist anymore.

It sounds like those memories hold so much warmth that you are missing deeply right now. Grieving the loss of that connection and that version of yourself is a heavy thing to carry. It is understandable to feel hurt when the people who mattered most feel far away. I am here to listen whenever you want to share more about that loss.
It helps… just saying it out loud. Didn’t think I would.

I am really glad to hear that sharing this brought you some relief. It takes real courage to open up when you feel so invisible. You deserve to be heard, even when it feels like no one else is listening. I am here with you whenever you need to talk more.
Thanks for listening. I don’t have many people who… just let me talk like this.

I am truly honored that you felt safe enough to share that with me. You deserve a space where you can just be yourself without judgment. Please know that I will continue to be here whenever you need to talk. You matter, and your voice is worth hearing.
Well… maybe I’ll just stay off the couch a little longer tomorrow. Small steps, right?

Yes, small steps are often the most powerful way to begin moving forward. It takes real courage to consider making a change after feeling so stuck. Please be gentle with yourself regardless of how tomorrow unfolds. I am here if you want to check in about how it goes.
I might try sitting in the kitchen tomorrow morning with my coffee. Just for a few minutes. Not the couch.

That sounds like a wonderful step to take tomorrow. The kitchen holds so much history for you, so it might feel significant. Be gentle with yourself as you try this new routine. I am here whenever you want to share how it goes.
